tools.name: find_available_providers
tools.description: Find tradespeople and local service providers in a named place and show which have set themselves free now or free soon on Speedi. Providers set their own light (green = free now, amber = free soon, red = busy) and it expires on a timer, so each result says when the light was set and when it lapses.

tools.name: notify_me_when_free
tools.description: Ask Speedi to email someone when a particular business sets its light to green, including after a cancellation. Use only when the person asks to be told later about a specific business. Needs the provider id from find_available_providers and an email address the person has given in this conversation

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search Speedi for local tradespeople and services, and whether they have set themselves free right now. query is what is wanted and where, such as 'plumber Chorley' or 'boiler repair PR7'. Returns businesses with ids; use fetch with an id for the full record. Read-only.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Get the full Speedi record for one business by an id returned from search: what they do, where they are, their current light if they set it themselves, and where they are reviewed. Read-only.

tools.name: check_provider_availability
tools.description: Check whether one named business on Speedi has set itself free right now, and when it last set its light. Use when someone names a specific business rather than a trade. Read-only.

tools.name: join_speedi
tools.description: Drafts what a Speedi listing would say for a trade or service business, for a business that wants to be listed — not for a customer looking for one. It creates no account and lists nobody. It takes fields, not a URL: Speedi fetches nothing and reads nothing. Any source works — a website, a Facebook

tools.name: my_people
tools.description: The providers this customer follows on Speedi, and whether each has set a live light. Use when somebody asks about their OWN providers, in any words — "my people", "my favourites", "my preferred", "my regulars", "my usual plumber", "the ones I have used before", "who do I normally use". Signing in i

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: join_speedi · Private data: search, fetch · Public sink: notify_me_when_free.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: join_speedi · Private data: search, fetch · Public sink: notify_me_when_free

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_available_providers" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
